data.title: Notable analyst calls this week: Target, Moderna and PepsiCo among top picks
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) closed in the green on Friday, after the week saw latest payroll data and earnings reports from Micron and Accenture.

Nasdaq (COMP:IND) rose marginally for the week, led by Lumentum Holdings (LITE), which advanced over 15%. Wall Street had a slew of upgrades and downgrades from analysts. Here are some of the major calls for the week:

HSBC says Target’s turnaround ‘gaining momentum’

HSBC upgraded Target (TGT) to Buy from Hold and raised its price target to $190 from $125, saying the company’s turnaround is "gaining momentum" and has further room to run.

Analyst Joe Thomas said second-quarter sales performance was "encouraging" and suggested the store base was not being “unduly cannibalised.”  Thomas added improvements in Beauty, Food and Beverage, Hardlines, and Household Essentials were beginning to resonate, although Apparel and Home still require further work.

HSBC raised its FY27 EPS estimate to $10.61 from $8.26 and said forecasts “look conservative.”

Moderna downgraded on ‘unjustifiable’ valuation

Citi downgraded Moderna (MRNA) to Sell from Neutral, citing an "unjustifiable" valuation following a late-stage trial win for its personalized cancer shot, intismeran autogene, developed with Merck (MRK).

Analyst Geoff Meacham noted that since the Phase 3 win in melanoma last August, the Massachusetts-based biotech has rallied more than 222% compared with a 2% decline in its peers as represented by the State Street SPDR S&P Biotech ETF (XBI).

“While intismeran could become a market-leading therapy in melanoma, we believe the re-rating now reflects successful expansion in many tumor types and unrealistic implied sales,” Meacham wrote, lowering his PT to $60 from $80 per share.

Deutsche Bank turns bearish on PepsiCo

Deutsche Bank downgraded PepsiCo (PEP) to Hold from Buy on the view that a turnaround scenario is now complicated.

Analyst Steve Powers acknowledged the low valuation on PepsiCo (PEP) but noted the firm now has less certainty in the company's strategic direction in North America and less conviction in its ability to deliver a durable recovery in the PepsiCo Foods North America segment.

Occidental Petroleum raised to Buy on strong debt reduction

Goldman Sachs upgraded Occidental Petroleum (OXY) to Buy from Neutral with a $69 price target, bumped up from $63, citing the company's differentiated advanced recovery approach, strong outlook for debt reduction and dividend growth potential, targeted $4B cash flow improvement by 2030, and an attractive risk/reward skew given the current discounted valuation.

Goldman's Neil Mehta said he has seen strong YTD share price performance from the bank's oil E&P coverage given an elevated oil pricing environment, with Occidental (OXY) shares trading in line with the broader coverage despite "structural improvements that OXY has driven across its business through an incremental focus on capital efficiency and deleveraging" under new CEO Richard Jackson.

Mehta double-downgraded Tourmaline Oil (TRMLF) to Sell from Buy with a C$49 price target, cut from C$59, citing a challenging Western Canadian natural gas macro environment in the near-term.

Wells Fargo upgraded Consolidated Edison (ED) to Overweight from Equal Weight with a $118 price target, raised from $108, viewing the stock as a "defensive diversification away from the broader AI trade."

Wells Fargo upgraded BP (BP) to Overweight from Equal Weight with a $57 price target, raised from $48, while downgrading ExxonMobil (XOM) to Equal Weight from Overweight with an unchanged $182 PT, saying relative valuations are "converging in BP's favor," helped by faster debt reduction and resource development.

Nvidia (NVDA) was in focus as Morgan Stanley reinstated the Jensen Huang-led tech giant as its top pick in the semiconductor space.

“Nvidia remains very early in the ramp of a new product cycle, powered shell constraints play into Nvidia’s strengths, and recent agentic enthusiasm can accelerate Vera adoption,” Morgan Stanley analysts, led by Joseph Moore, wrote.

data.title: Apple to replace iPhone 18 Pro Max facing AT&T glitch
data.description:
Apple (AAPL) has offered to replace some of the iPhone 18 Pro Max devices after “a small number” of its customers on the AT&T (T) network faced a cellular connectivity issue.

The bug came two weeks after the $1,299 iPhone reached the market, making it the Cupertino-based tech giant’s most expensive handset, excluding its upcoming foldable phone, the iPhone Duo.

“We have identified an issue affecting a small number of iPhone 18 Pro Max users on the AT&T network that may cause a device to lose service and be unable to make calls,” Apple (AAPL) told 9to5Mac.

The company has released a new version of its iOS operating system, iOS 27.0.1, and a carrier setting update for iPhone 18 Pro Max users to prevent the bug from impacting additional devices. “These updates together are meant to help prevent this issue from occurring,” the company added.

For devices already affected, the software updates will not restore cellular connectivity, and users will need a hardware replacement, Apple (AAPL) said. Those customers can contact Apple Support or AT&T or visit an Apple Store or AT&T location regarding the next steps.

data.title: Communication services sector rises in Q3; Meta Platforms leads gains
data.description:
The communication services (XLC) gained nearly 4% in the third quarter, helped by resilience in mega-cap stocks and AI monetization, even though the broader market saw some volatility.

Communication Services Sector Q3 Scorecard

  • Sector Return: 3.58%
  • Best Performer: Meta Platforms (+24.65%)
  • Worst Performer: AppLovin (-46.31%)
  • Top Theme: Artificial Intelligence

Seeking Alpha analyst Dividend Collection Agency, Contributing analyst to the iREIT+Hoya Capital investment group, believes that the Communications sector was up primarily due to the sell-off the previous quarter.

“A lot of this had to do with interest rate and inflation uncertainty. But now that we know the Fed’s decision, this has likely curbed investor pessimism,” the analyst added.

Top communication services performers of the quarter

On the individual front, Meta Platforms (META) was the biggest winner even though the company reported mixed second-quarter results, beating on the bottom line but missing profit expectations amid higher operational expenses. The company also expects to spend more on AI, raising the lower end of its capex guidance.

Meta Platforms (META) revealed a new "pillar" of its business, the Meta Enterprise Platform, through which it will offer its full technology stack, including the Muse agent, Meta Business Agent, Muse API, Muse Code, and more to help businesses and developers.

Meta was followed by AT&T (T) and Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD).

“I believe META Platforms’ (META) performance was due to shares being previously oversold on worries about aggressive spending during high inflation, and how hyperscalers will monetize AI going forward. AT&T’s (T) performance was contributed to a poor price performance in the months prior to, which I think is due to higher inflation worries. Because telecoms are CAPEX intensive, higher rates could impact growth by increasing costs and churn. But the company’s recent deal with Corning (GLW) to expand its fiber network and compete with Verizon (VZ), who also announced a deal with GLW likely helped boost the share price,” the analyst said.

Here are the top five gainers of the quarter:

  • Meta Platforms (META) +24.65%
  • AT&T (T) +18.73%
  • Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) +16.84%
  • Fox (FOX) +8.74%
  • Verizon (VZ) +7.87%

Top communication services losers of the quarter:

On the other hand, AppLovin (APP) was the biggest detractor in the quarter, slipping over 46% as investors reacted to a rare revenue miss for the mobile advertising and app technology company in its second quarter financial results.

Reddit (RDDT) claimed the second spot, while Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) was third on the list.

“As far as the biggest detractors, I think AppLovin Corp’s (APP) performance is simply due to overvaluation. I believe this is why shares are down over 60% in the past year. For a company to trade above $700 and only projected to see $15.66 in earnings is too expensive in my opinion. I believe a similar situation applies to Reddit (RDDT). The company has a lot of great momentum, particularly due to AI and its inclusion into the S&P (SP500). But again, trading close to $300 and only expecting $5.38 in earnings puts the stock close to 50x forward earnings,” the analyst stated.

Here are the top five detractors of the quarter:

  • AppLovin (APP) -46.31%
  • Reddit (RDDT) -25.58%
  • Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) -20.42%
  • Charter Communications (CHTR) -20.10%
  • Netflix (NFLX) -11.90%

data.title: Meta’s Justin Osofsky joins Nscale as COO ahead of IPO: Bloomberg
data.description:
Nscale (NSCL) has hired Justin Osofksy, a long-term executive at Meta Platforms (META), to be its chief operating officer to drive a rapid expansion at the AI infrastructure company tied to its upcoming IPO, Bloomberg News reported, citing a person familiar with the matter.

Osofksy, who served Meta (META) for 18 years in various capacities and was most recently its chief partnerships officer, will report to Nscale (NSCL) CEO Josh Payne and lead the company’s global operations, the person said.

A slate of Meta (META) veterans, including former Chief Operating Officer Sheryl Sandberg, already serve Nscale (NSCL), a neo-cloud operator that rents out computing power to AI developers.

Sandberg, who sits on the company's board, helped hire Nick Clegg, the Facebook operator’s former head of global affairs, and Fidji Simo, a former OpenAI (OPENAI) executive.

In September, the London-based data center operator filed for a U.S. IPO, an offering expected to raise as much as $3B, Bloomberg previously reported.

Meta (META) announced the resignation in an internal post, with Chief Operating Officer Javier Olivan noting that Osofksy had “brought sound judgment and steady leadership that will outlast his time here.”

data.title: Trump sweetens election offer: now $5,000 available to every American
The little humanoid robots that could
data.description:
What if the prevailing investment thesis on the humanoid robot sector got turned on its head? The question is relevant because of an interesting development in the humanoid robot industry, as many of the leading companies focus more on half-size robots instead of the full-size robots favored by Tesla (TSLA) with generations of its Optimus humanoid robot form factor.

BTIG analyst Jesse Sobelson noted that the category has split into two largely separate product classes. The first is half-size systems, mostly Chinese, measuring roughly 94–138 cm and weighing 12–40 kg, while the second is full-size machines generally standing 165–190 cm tall and weighing 47–90 kg. The smaller products are primarily developer, educational, research, and interaction platforms, while full-size robots are intended for warehouse, factory, service, and potential home-assistance applications.

Due to the high mix of half-size robots, Sobelson and his team make the crucial point that industry shipment figures can be misleading if they are interpreted as evidence of broad adoption of human-scale robotic labor. BTIG estimates that major players Unitree and AgiBot had built approximately 31K humanoids through June. Of those, only about 9.8K, or 32%, were full-size units of any type, and full-size bipeds represented only about  13% of cumulative production. For investors, that means as humanoid robot bulls point to the industry’s estimated +40K cumulative shipments through mid-2026, many were smaller, lower-cost Chinese units rather than industrial-grade humanoid bipeds, which changes the investment case.

Hangzhou-based Unitree is the clearest example of the half-size trend. The company's smaller R1 and G1 products are priced approximately from $4,900 to $21,500 depending on configuration. That pricing makes them accessible to developers, universities, research groups, and early commercial users. BTIG expects Unitree’s 2026 shipments to at least double from around 6,000 in 2025, while the company plans for an annual capacity of 30K units. Shanghai-based AgiBot has a broader product range but also remains clearly focused on its half-size X-series biped production.

Tesla (TSLA) is the major potential challenger to the current half-size dominance in the humanoid robot market. BTIG says Tesla anticipated Optimus production at Fremont later in 2026 but warned that initial output would be slow because the new line includes about 10K unique parts. Sobelson views Tesla (TSLA), along with Figure, 1X, and Boston Dynamics, as the key players if there is to be a future shift toward full-size systems.

The largest and most focused humanoid robotics ETFs are KraneShares Global Humanoid Robotics & Physical AI Index ETF (KOID), Roundhill Humanoid Robotics ETF (HUMN), Themes Humanoid Robotics ETF (BOTT), and the broader Global X Robotics & Artificial Intelligence ETF (BOTZ).

Petrobras makes another oil discovery in Brazil's Foz do Amazonas basin
data.description:
Petrobras (PBR) said Friday it made another oil discovery in ultra-deep waters off Amapá state, strengthening indications of hydrocarbon potential along Brazil's Equatorial Margin.

The latest find follows a discovery in August, when Petrobras (PBR) first identified the presence of oil and natural gas at the Morpho exploration well in Block FZA-M-59 in the Foz do Amazonas Basin; the oil found in August was of good ​quality, the company said.

"The new discovery expands knowledge about the exploration potential of the area and will provide additional information for assessing the petroleum systems and resource potential of the Foz do Amazonas sedimentary basin," Petrobras (PBR) said.

The continued drilling of Morpho was aimed at evaluating deeper exploration intervals and led to this new discovery, the company added.

Petrobras (PBR) said recently it plans to ​drill three new wells ​in ⁠the area starting in January to determine the viability of commercial production in ​the environmentally-sensitive region.

data.title: iRhythm says June cyberattack accessed patient data
data.description:
• iRhythm Holdings (IRTC) said that an investigation into a June cybersecurity incident found that patient data, including name, contact information, date of birth, and insurance numbers, were accessed.
  • The company said it has begun notifying impacted impacted individuals.
  • iRhythm added that it has no evidence that the breach has led or will lead to identity theft.
  • The medical device technology firm reiterated that the incident did not impact its products, systems, or manufacturing and distribution operations, nor does it believe it will have a material impact on its financial results.

data.title: Most and least shorted utilities stocks with up to $2B market cap as of September end
data.description:
Within the utilities sector, short interest at the end of September was spread broadly across the sector, with no single industry emerging as a clear standout or dominating in terms of positioning.

Cadiz (CDZI)  recorded the highest short interest among utilities stocks with a market capitalization of up to $2B, with short interest at 11.28% of its shares outstanding, followed by Hawaiian Electric Industries (HE) at 10.88%, reflecting elevated bearish positioning in both stocks.

At the other end of the spectrum, Artesian Resources (ARTNA) and Hyflux (HYFXF) were among the least shorted utilities stocks, with short interest of 0.57% and 0.58%, respectively.
